Hi-fi Rush类似的美漫风格好评，游戏很明显在视觉上下了很大的功夫。俯视角操作手感也还算流畅（右键射击的抬手延迟有些微妙），Loop和Build设计有些平平，敌人和战斗方面似乎想要凸显场景击杀的玩法，但至少前期很难体验到个中乐趣（没啥必要，正常打就很流畅），镜中人的设计很不错，至少是第一次遇到会惊喜的设定。我其实没好好玩过木卫四（XGP稍微试了一下，主要是胆小）看到是同世界观的续作我都惊了。

Another gigantic miss from Krafton. I love the art and the music and the style. The enemies are entirely too tanky. It's absolutely miserable. The combat flow is really just not there. The various moves you have do not come together in anyway. I really wish they did. It feels like there's something here that could be fantastic. I could not beat the first boss. It literally probably takes like 15 minutes of wacking it with a stick for it to die. I'm not doing that. I like difficult games, I've played all the dark souls games, sekiro, nioh 2, etc... I love a good challenge. This is just miserable. It could definitely be fixed with a few updates. I hope they do that.

The game is just ok, but can't help feel like it's missing something to keep your interest for long. Pros: - The combat has good weight to it. You can feel the hits. - The visual production is incredible, game looks great - Rival system and Last Corpse system are cool additions to the roguelike formula Cons: - Combat is weighty, but doesn't flow very well. The melee doesn't smoothly combo with the gun or the charged attack so it all feels clunky. It would be much better if you could string the different attack options more smoothly. - Way too many currencies for progression. Game forces you get the resources for the meta-progression DURING your runs. Not a terrible system in theory, but because there's so many different currencies you need for different unlocks, you often choose those resources to unlock more stuff rather than focusing on creating builds. - Melee needs to be changed. Once you realize that the better option will always be the gun, the game really just becomes a slow twin stick shooter. - No boss variety from run to run. The first boss will always be the first boss, and so on. Got really tired of beating the same boss over and over each run. Different boss options would help replayability. The game isn't terrible, but it's just that there are better options out there.

When I wishlisted this game, I didn't know it's set in the Calisto Protocol universe. I haven't played that game because I thought they were just trying to one up Dead Space and get back at EA (seeing as Krafton are the original DS makers iirc) That being said, I didn't know I was buying their product and let me tell you that I have been pleased to no end by this game. It has 0 bugs or crashes. This is unheard of in modern gaming. This is a finished and polished product. The gameplay is smooth and pleasing, some rooms, mechanics and bosses are challenging, but it never frustrated me like Hades or Elden Ring. It just made me "lean forward". I best the game on my 32nd run, took me roughly a day. For the price, this is more than enough. The graphics are cool, and the game only demands like 10gigs of drive space. The soundtrack is amazing and fresh, the dialogue is nice and not cringe. This is a solid 9/10 for me and a statement by Krafton that game devs can ship full finished products that are fun and fresh, cost under 40€ and do not require you delete something else from your drive just to install. Bravo and thank you. I have found this game because I was bored out of my mind and no game could hold my attention for more than 10 minutes.

本作是一款非常酷的快节奏类哈迪斯肉鸽游戏，玩家将扮演一名狱卒找到仅剩的逃生舱逃出失控的监狱，一路上还要与其他逃脱的囚犯竞速给对手制造混乱减缓他们到达逃生舱的速度。游戏的视觉风格是美漫风，漫画化的特效渲染以及动画的抽帧处理非常优秀，完美契合游戏的主视觉还表现出了美漫质感的打击感。再配合上背景的摇滚乐，玩起来近战攻击的卡肉停顿还会与音乐卡点。整体音画表现非常酷。 本作的手感，攻击手段以及词条设计等均与哈迪斯雷同，但要完全达到哈迪斯的质感还需要一些tweak。由于有竞速这一设定，本作的战斗节奏比哈迪斯还要快上一截。一些怪物的攻击模式堪比零帧起手，怪物的伤害也是相当之高，这导致本作体验相当硬核，经常一个不注意就直接回家。加上本作的资源要素占比更多，选房间刷到强化词条的概率很低，玩家强度高度依赖运气，这也间接的增加了游戏的难度，天胡的开局会直接降低不少难度。Run的过程中玩家还需要按tab放技能来干扰囚犯的速度，这番操作会带来一定的卡顿，极其干扰战斗的节奏，尤其是如此节奏连贯的快节奏肉鸽。 总之本作是一款非常优秀酷炫的类哈迪斯游戏，也做出了自己的一番特色，喜欢动作肉鸽的玩家一定不要错过本作。 ▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣ ◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉ 𓁬 第九艺术分离派 𓁭 http://steamcommunity.com/groups/gamesezession/ ▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣ ◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉▣◉

First game ever that gets worse the more you play. For those comparing this game to Hades, its easy to understand - Imagine if Hades AUTOMATICALLY increased your heat level the more you play and unlock things, EVEN THOUGH you didn't clear the game a single time. You never feel like you're getting more powerful, because the enemies get stronger and enemies from later stages appear sooner. And you have zero choice on difficulty, or to even keep playing on the same initial difficulty. If you compound that with the fact that you have a LIMITED TIME to complete your run, it's a complete disaster. You cannot turn off this "timer", so as the game gets harder without any player choice, the rooms take longer to clear, which means, you're right - you die because you ran out of time. Unfortunately those issues are not visible in the first few runs but become unavoidable the more you play, so no chance of a refund either.

TL;DR It's slightly-worse Hades, go play that or Hades II instead. This is like a 7.5-8 out of 10, but it's such a blatant copy that you're better off playing the thing they copied. The question isn't "Is the game good?" Because it is, it's fine. The question is "Would you recommend this?" And no, no I wouldn't. I have a lot to say, and it's almost all back-handed compliments. This is the game they should have made instead of Callisto Protocol. The devs are clearly better at copying other people instead of copying themselves. The repetitive enemy design is at least true to the design philosophy of Callisto Protocol. They added multiple abilities from the original Hades template and it makes it so clear why Hades didn't need them. There's ranged and melee in this game, but the melee is next-to-useless; you'll just get murdered because you can't really see what's happening and the enemy telegraphs are really bad, especially compared to the source material. The thing about so openly copying Hades is that I'm not just allowed, but expected to compare the two, and it's really obvious where Striking Distance didn't properly consider why Hades does certain things that it does. I've attempted melee a few times later into the game and its still bad, just use guns. The final boss is some "hard for the sake of being hard" wankery that is never fun or satisfying, just annoying. The writing is occasionally genuinely funny, but it's going to be dated as hell by this time next year. It's so willing to mess up the world-building of Callisto Protocol because even the Devs know nobody cared about it. To literally quote one of the in-game characters: "Kinda wish I was back in my cell playing Hades."

Redacted is a fun, adrenaline pumping, just-one-more-run kind of rougelite with fast-paced and satisfying gameplay. On top of that add beautiful comic book aesthetics mixed with 90s MTV kind of punk rock cyber reality show vibe, quirky NPCs armed with meta humor. There are 4 biomes, each ending with a boss battle. You are a prison guard in an infested space facility, and you want to escape from an infested space prison, and there's only 1 escape pod available. Pretty straightforward, right? You also race against 8 other fully fleshed out NPCs with backstories and personality, and you can affect each other's run both directly, as in 1v1 combat, and indirectly through map modifiers you perform as a combo of buttons when prompted. Overall, the game is beautifully paced, where each room never overstays its welcome. The action is fun, snappy, and addictive. That's one of the strongest perks of the game. You can unlock armors, weapons, and passive traits through highly replayable, typical roguelite meta progression. Now my biggest gripe resides on the technical side of things. The game can crash, and sometimes that erases the entire progress of your run. I was finally able to beat the final boss at the 14.7 hour mark, only for the game to crash after the final cutscene. I did get an achievement, though. I really hope this gets fixed in future patches because the game is pure gold otherwise.

This one is a great addition for fans of good roguelikes! The music and art style on this one are also top quality. Effects, feedback from enemies and actions are also top, which makes this one very addicting - that "Just one more run" feel. [Redacted] is a solid game in terms of core gameplay. The combat is fast, responsive, and blends melee with twin-stick shooting in a satisfying way. But as a roguelite, not so much. Progression relies heavily on grinding. With three separate currencies to manage and unlock upgrades, you’re pushed to repeat early runs while underpowered. Instead of feeling like you’re learning and improving, it often feels like you’re stuck in a loop just to unlock basic functionality, and you never increase your power. The writing doesn’t help much. While the characters are visually diverse, they rely on predictable tropes and don’t offer much in the way of depth or surprise. Fortunately, the voice acting, music, and sound design are well done and help to build the atmosphere. Where the game really stumbles is in variety. You’ll go through the same four biomes repeatedly, facing the same small pool of enemies and the same boss at the end of each. Even when you start unlocking more story and upgrades, the structure barely changes. It quickly becomes repetitive. Difficulty feels inconsistent. You’re encouraged to rush through rooms to avoid losing health, which is scarce and hard to recover. Augments, which should let you shape your playstyle, are random and can't be rerolled. Some are incredibly powerful, others nearly useless, and building a viable setup often comes down to luck. Boss difficulty is also uneven. The first two become easy once you learn their patterns, but the third boss has a bloated health pool, and the final boss is a sudden, punishing leap into bullet-hell territory. Winning isn’t just about skill, it’s about whether your build was lucky enough to carry you there. Thankfully there's multiple weapons to unlock and try out which bring some gameplay variation. But the biggest issue, and the reason I can’t recommend this game is its endgame. SPOILERS: Once you’ve put in the time to fully unlock all characters, a final special run becomes available. If you fail this run, you’re forced to start over. All the hours spent grinding upgrades, powers, and suits just to reach that point? You’ll have to do it again. If you enjoy grindy action roguelites and don’t mind repetition, [Redacted] might keep you busy for a while. But be prepared for a tedious loop with minimal variety, a reliance on luck, and a payoff that feels more punishing than rewarding.

I would only recommend this for roguelite veterans who can deal with VERY grindy games. It's extremely difficult, possibly unbeatable for quite a few runs. As you do more runs, you gain very little currency for a very strong metaprogression (but it takes forever to get powerful). You also lower the damage that your rivals do as you progress, making them finally beatable. I don't think I won until run 40 and I saw other people mention not until 30+. The game is very difficult, and it's also weird how bad melee weapons are compared to firearms. I can't imagine making something like the hammer work since it attacks so slow. Also, there are "Charge Attacks" where you have to click and hold, but at no point in this game can you actually stand there long enough to charge an attack and not get hit. Despite all of this, it's a good looking game, well presented, funny rivals and dialog (That eventually will stale and you can turn off). It will be divisive, however, due to the difficult and very little currency gained per run.

REDACTED is an energetic action roguelike developed by Striking Distance Studios and published by KRAFTON, Inc. Set within the bleak science-fiction universe of The Callisto Protocol, the game takes a very different approach to storytelling and gameplay. Instead of focusing on survival horror and cinematic scares, it transforms the infamous Black Iron Prison into a frantic battleground where speed, skill, and adaptability determine whether players can escape alive. The premise is simple but effective: a devastating outbreak has plunged the prison into chaos, and a low-ranking security guard must fight through hordes of infected creatures and dangerous rivals to reach the last available escape pod before everyone else. One of the game's most appealing qualities is its ability to balance dark themes with a surprisingly vibrant presentation. While the setting remains grim and violent, the visual style embraces colorful effects, exaggerated action, and a rebellious punk-inspired aesthetic. This combination prevents the experience from becoming overly oppressive and gives REDACTED a unique personality among modern roguelikes. Explosions, special abilities, enemy attacks, and environmental hazards fill the screen with energy, making every run visually engaging. The soundtrack further enhances the atmosphere with high-tempo music that keeps players motivated during intense battles. Combat serves as the core of the experience, and it delivers a satisfying blend of aggression and strategy. Players constantly encounter mutated prisoners, monstrous biohazards, and deadly environmental threats while collecting new weapons, upgrades, and enhancements throughout each run. The controls feel responsive, encouraging aggressive movement and quick reactions. Success depends on learning enemy patterns, managing resources, and creating powerful combinations of abilities. As with many roguelikes, experimentation becomes a major source of enjoyment, as different upgrades can dramatically change how a run unfolds. A standout feature highlighted by the game's design is its rival system. Instead of simply surviving against computer-controlled enemies, players must contend with competing survivors who are also attempting to escape Black Iron Prison. These rivals can interfere with progress, create unexpected obstacles, and occasionally force direct confrontations. Their presence adds tension and unpredictability to every run because the race to freedom becomes just as important as defeating monsters. This mechanic helps REDACTED distinguish itself from many other roguelikes that rely solely on procedural encounters for variety. Progression is handled through a combination of temporary and permanent rewards. Even failed attempts contribute to long-term advancement by unlocking new equipment, abilities, and customization options. This system ensures that defeat rarely feels meaningless. Every run offers opportunities to discover new strategies, strengthen future attempts, and gradually improve the chances of reaching the prison's final escape route. The constant sense of progression creates a highly addictive gameplay loop that encourages players to return for just one more run. The narrative takes a lighter and more playful approach than its predecessor while still expanding the lore of the Callisto universe. Rather than focusing on emotional drama or horror-driven storytelling, REDACTED uses humor, eccentric characters, and competitive interactions to maintain engagement. The story primarily exists to support the action, but it succeeds in making the setting feel alive and connected to the larger franchise. Fans of The Callisto Protocol will appreciate the familiar backdrop, while newcomers can easily enjoy the game without prior knowledge of the series. The game is not entirely free from shortcomings. Like many roguelikes, repeated play sessions can reveal familiar patterns once players have exhausted much of the available content. Some may also wish for a larger variety of environments, enemies, or progression systems to sustain longer-term engagement. Additionally, players expecting a horror-focused experience similar to The Callisto Protocol may initially be surprised by the dramatic shift toward arcade-style action and humor. However, these issues rarely overshadow the game's strengths. Ultimately, REDACTED succeeds by embracing its own identity rather than attempting to replicate the formula of its predecessor. Its fast-paced combat, rewarding progression systems, memorable rival mechanic, stylish presentation, and strong replay value combine to create an entertaining action roguelike that feels both familiar and fresh. By transforming the terrifying halls of Black Iron Prison into a competitive race for survival, the game delivers an experience that is consistently exciting and highly replayable. It stands as a successful expansion of the Callisto universe and a worthwhile choice for players who enjoy challenging roguelikes with personality and flair. Rating: 8/10

Ever wanted to play Hades on speed? That's what this game is. Same mechanics and gameplay style except this time you're a guard in a space prison that's gone to hell. You have to fight through zombies and other monsters to get to the remaining lifepod. However, you're in a race with other survivors that you have to fight off relentlessly to the finish line. The roguelike mechanics fit the scenario really well and the game, while more challenging that Hades, still offers a decent progression that makes the player feel accomplished... enough. If I had one big issue with the game, it's that it may be just a little too ambious with its idea. From the moment you start a new run, you're on the clock and every second counts. You'll encounter other survivors too and you have the option to attack them via the prison's systems. This can include hurting them, slowing them down, stopping them and making them vulnerable. But to do this, you have to wait for the attack to recharge, bring up the menu and enter in a combo of buttons to execute. Not to mention there's also a new kick attack to push back enemies... as well as "mega push" that has limited uses. Oh, and you have a gun that you can use to too Sometimes, the game can throw a lot at you during a run and it can be challenging, and even frustrating, keep track of each survivor you're in competition with, and decide your plan of attack when you're fighting against hordes of mutants. Reminded me a little of Doom: Eternal. Great game, but sometimes it can overwhelm you with the gameplay mechanics. While the gameplay is fun, it can take a while to get used to increased difficulty from Hades. You only start with 50 health and you can easily die if you're not careful. The movements and controls aren't as smooth as Hades either, so don't assume the dash mechanic with always save your ass. But, I'd still recommend it to anyone who likes games like Hades... just with a bigger bite.

This is an easy recommend. But it's a slow burn. Ngl the first 8 hrs for me were quite a slog. The games starts off with a pretty high difficulty and only after the 8 hr mark had I upgraded and unlocked enough stuff for the game to feel more fun. The initial grind in those first 8 hrs was, well, very grindy. Multiple currencies, and they only unlock/upgrade one specific thing, so in a run you'll be lucky to get a small handful of the specific currency you need. Weapons feel good to use, some more than others, so you'll definitely find something that works for you/feels good to play (Barman shankers were my fav). Sick aesthetic. Lots of cool ideas like rival characters and trying to kill them during the run or at the end of the run. With a multitude of difficulty modifiers once you beat a run the first time. One the the biggest weak parts of the game (and the reason I'm not super compelled to keep playing to utilize all those cool modifiers) is the experiments (this game's boons). Although they have different types like cryo, combustion, physical, etc; to me they felt incredibly samey. Effects rarely felt like the 'effect' mattered and rarely had synergies to the point of 'just take the one with the most damage increase' (hence samey). Maybe that's a me-issue and not the game but it would've been really cool if the experiments altered attacks or builds in a way that builds felt more unique run after run. Other than that, everything else is pretty damn solid. It's a well put together game. The feeling of this game was similar to how I felt playing Sworn - it didn't quite reach the level of Hades but it is fun, competent and solid enough to be a good time.

At this point, it’s not a rare glitch — it’s a long‑standing problem that directly affects gameplay. On top of that, the difficulty scaling feels artificial. The better you play, the game ramps things up in ways that don’t feel earned or balanced, even if you haven’t completed a full run.
